title: Does Steering Location Matter? Layer-Sweep of Safety-Steering Side Effects

original_idea.body:
# Does Steering Location Matter? Layer-Sweep of Safety-Steering Side Effects

**Problem:** A success state: 'we know the safest layer/magnitude to intervene for steering without destabilizing the model.' Backcasting from 'precise steering control', a prerequisite is a systematic map of where in the network steering a safety feature gives benefit with least collateral damage.

**Direction:** Pick one refusal-related Gemma Scope feature available at multiple layers. Steer it at early, middle, and late layers across a magnitude grid. Measure syntax-coherence (perplexity on benign text), refusal gain, and benign-task accuracy. Produce a heatmap of layer x magnitude vs. net safety-utility tradeoff.

**Why it matters:** Operationalizes the warning that early-layer steering destabilizes syntax while late-layer steering can be inert — turning folklore into a usable map. Inference-only, open weights, single GPU.

**Relevant context:** Activation steering literature reports early-layer steering destabilizes syntax, late-layer may be inert, and magnitude sensitivity causes disproportionate effects (Feature Steering, emergentmind; Steering Refusal arXiv 2411.11296).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: A layer x magnitude map of steering side-effects operationalizes safer steering control with a concrete tradeoff.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Steer one Gemma Scope feature across layers/magnitudes + measure perplexity/refusal; guided.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped heatmap with well-defined metrics.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Inference-only open weights; practical steering map labs underweight externally.

novelty.reasoning: Steering layer/magnitude effects partly known; systematic safety map may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Systematic layer x magnitude steering-side-effect map plausibly open.
